sections.name: summary
sections.value: The task detail for one phase. The plan document carries the overview and links here; each task row carries one link to its own `done_when` assertion list, and the row's progress is computed from that list rather than typed into it. Every assertion names its instrument: a backpressure row, or the literal `not-applicable` with the real instrument in its note.

value.title: Resolution fixture corpus covering every schema-layer failure class, each with a good twin
Schema package model and deep-scan resolution with first-hit-wins precedence
Declarations: field-level custom enums and per-schema gate-terminal sets
Flip `dd validate` live over the real resolver, the core engine, and the depth walk
`dd schema list` and `dd schema show` bodies, with resolved paths always visible
Exemplar `builder/*` schema packages carrying the workshop shapes
Baked docs compiled into the CLI, with a two-way drift gate
Leaf rulings recorded before their consumers land
Validation and proof: slice suite, full suite, architecture baseline, recorded live run

tk-0201.assertion: Every schema-layer failure class has at least one bad fixture and one good twin.
A README maps each fixture to its class and its twin, so the corpus explains itself.
The precedence-chain fixture proves first-hit-wins order exactly, not merely that resolution succeeds.

tk-0202.assertion: A qualified name comes from the folder path, never from the file, so a copied package cannot misreport its identity.
All hits are recorded, not just the winner: every shadowed duplicate is reported with its path.
A same-root duplicate is a hard error while a cross-root duplicate is a reported shadow.
The scan's depth bound is a named constant with a recorded ruling and a fixture that crosses it.
tk-0202.note: Found by review, not by the original pass: the bound existed and was silent.

tk-0203.assertion: A custom enum validates end-to-end through the real resolver.
tk-0203.note: the declarations suite drives a custom enum end to end through the real resolver; no backpressure row states the declaration layer

tk-0203.assertion: A declared gate-terminal set changes what derived state calls complete.
tk-0203.note: the derived-state tests cover it; the toolbelt has no row for gate-terminal declarations

tk-0203.assertion: Two different gate-terminal sets bound to state fields are refused at declaration time.
tk-0203.note: a planted-bad declaration fixture fires at resolution; not a backpressure criterion

tk-0204.assertion: A good document exits ok and an ERROR-class document exits with its own issue code.
tk-0204.note: the validate act's good/bad fixture pair; bp-0901 is about a plan document, not the verb

tk-0204.assertion: Depth 2 and depth 3 genuinely differ on a three-hop corpus, through the CLI.
tk-0204.note: the three-hop depth fixture in the CLI suite

tk-0204.assertion: Direct invocation never skips a document: a known-bad fixture still fails when named explicitly.

tk-0205.assertion: Both verbs print the resolved file path, always.
Shadowing is visible in both verbs, with the full chain in `show`.

tk-0206.assertion: The packages resolve by real deep scan from the repository root.
The plan schema declares the two signpost link columns as typed links, not as text.
Each package ships the custom-type adapters its schema needs.
tk-0206.note: the render goldens fail if an adapter a schema names is missing

tk-0207.assertion: `dd docs list` shows every baked doc with its description and `dd docs get` returns the content.
The drift gate is proven in both directions: exit 0 on a clean tree, exit 1 on injected drift.
tk-0207.note: A control demonstrated only on a green tree is not a control.

tk-0207.assertion: An unknown doc id returns its own error code rather than an empty result.
tk-0207.note: the dd docs get error-path test; bp-0801 watches drift, not the unknown-id path

tk-0208.assertion: Every leaf ruling was recorded with its rationale before the code that consumes it landed.
tk-0208.note: human review of the ruling ledger's dates against the commits that consume them

tk-0209.assertion: The phase's own slice suite is green with the parallel phases absent.
tk-0209.note: the slice suite is run with the parallel phases absent as a one-off demonstration; the durable residue is the suite itself

tk-0209.assertion: Suites that spawn the CLI are proven from both sanctioned invocations.
tk-0209.note: both sanctioned invocations are exercised by the quality gate

tk-0209.assertion: The architecture baseline is unmoved: dd adds no new violation.
The repository-root invocation of the suite is exercised by the quality gate, not merely sanctioned by a config file.
tk-0209.note: the quality gate runs the repository-root invocation on every commit
tk-0209.receipt: Recorded in the phase-2 log: "left to the retro / P5 checks conversation, per the PM's ruling not to decide it inside a fix round".
